title: Single-sister labeling in the C. elegans germline using the nucleotide analog EdU
protocol: Collect 50–100 age matched L4 or young adult (12–24 h post-L4) C. elegans hermaphrodites for EdU incorporation.
Pipette M9/Triton X onto a plate of L4 worms.
Aspirate M9/Triton X with L4 worms.
Transfer M9/Triton X and L4 worms to a fresh 1.5 ml tube.
Spin down worms.
Wash once with M9/Triton X.
Aspirate 40 μl of M9/Triton containing the worms into a fresh 1.5 ml tube.
Add 60 μl of 10 mM EdU to the tube.
Vortex gently to mix worms and EdU.
Place worms and EdU onto a nutator.
Transfer population of worms to a tube for EdU labeling.
Add 1 mL M9/Triton X solution to the plate.
Swirl gently 3–5 times and aspirate the liquid with the worms into a clean 1.5 mL tube.
Spin down worms using a tabletop centrifuge for 30 s at 2,500 g.
Aspirate as much of the supernatant as possible without disturbing the loose worm pellet.
Wash an additional time with 1 mL M9/Triton X to remove excess bacteria.
Transfer the bottom 60 μL of M9/Triton X which contains the age-matched worms to a clean 1.5 mL tube.
Add 40 μL of 10 mM EdU in water to the worms (final concentration: 4 mM EdU in 100 μL total volume).
Vortex gently.
Transfer tube with worms to a nutator for 40 min at 20°C–25°C at 80 RPM.
Wash worms 2× with 1 mL M9/Triton X.
Spin down the sample as previously indicated.
Aspirate all but approximately 50–100 μL of solution without disturbing the worm pellet.
Transfer the 50–100 μL containing worms to a fresh NGM plate.
Let the plate dry for 10–30 minutes or until all liquid is absorbed.
Place the plates in an incubator set at the desired temperature.
Note the time as the start of the chase period.
Prepare Fix solution using gloves in a well-ventilated area or fume hood.
Place a Coplin jar with methanol in a −20°C freezer and place a metal block on dry ice.
Dissect age-matched adults.
Place a coverslip on top of a glass slide under a dissection microscope.
Fit a scalpel blade into a scalpel holder.
Transfer worms by picking into the EBT solution.
Dissect C. elegans gonads using the scalpel to remove the head or tail of the animal.
Add fix solution to the worms in EBT.
Aspirate as much liquid as possible (∼45 μL), being careful not to aspirate the worms.
Gently touch the bonded side of the slide to the coverslip.
Transfer the slide, coverslip facing up, onto an ice block cooled on dry ice.
Insert a razor blade under a corner of the coverslip and gently pry to flick off the coverslip.
Transfer the slide into 100% methanol cooled to −20°C.
Transfer slides to a fresh Coplin jar of PBST.
Pipette 30 μL of EBT onto the coverslip.
Pick 10–30 worms into the drop of EBT and allow 30–60 seconds for worms to anesthetize.
Cut the heads and/or tails off the worms to extrude the gonads.
After all animals are dissected, pipette 30 μL of Fix solution into the drop of dissected worms.
Pipette up and down 3–5 times to mix the solutions and help release more gonads.
Leave the Fix solution on for 1 minute.
Aspirate excess liquid, leaving as little as possible remaining (∼15 μL) while trying to keep the worm carcasses separated from one another.
Pick up the drop by lightly touching a HistoBond microscope slide on top of it.
Place the sample on an ice block for more than one minute.
Form ice crystals between the slide and the coverslip.
Keep the slides on ice until all samples are dissected (approximately 30-60 minutes).
Insert a razor blade under the edge of the coverslip to flick it off carefully.
Handle glass shards with care; collect broken coverslips and place them in the glass waste.
Place the slide immediately into -20°C methanol, incubate for one minute.
Transfer slides to a fresh Coplin jar containing PBST at 20-25°C using forceps.
Wash slides three times in PBST (each wash lasting 5-10 minutes).
Block slides in 1× Roche Block in a Coplin jar for 30 minutes to 2 hours at 20-25°C, or overnight at 4°C.
Save 100 μL per slide for the first antibody solution buffer.
Block slides in 1× Roche Block.
Add 100 μL of primary antibody solution to a parafilm square (one square per slide).
Remove slide from PBST and gently dry the back of the slide, taking care not to disturb the worms stuck to the front of the slide.
Prepare the humid chamber by wetting a paper towel and placing it on the bottom of a perforated chamber with a lid.
Gently touch the slide (worms down) to the primary antibody. The parafilm should stick to the slide.
Incubate the slides, parafilm side up, in a humid chamber with the lid closed.
Transfer slides to a fresh, fully filled Coplin jar of PBST, allowing the parafilm squares to float to the top.
Mix by flicking the tube or gently pipetting up and down for primary antibody solution preparation.
Do not vortex the primary antibody solution.
Mix 15 mM sterile HCl with human recombinant leptin.
Add 7.5 mM sterile NaOH to achieve a stock concentration of 1.25 mg/ml.
Apply 100 μL of primary antibody solution to parafilm squares without forming bubbles.
Carefully wipe slides (avoid touching the worm carcasses) and ensure all carcasses are immersed in liquid on the parafilm with antibody.
Incubate slides in a humid chamber for 2 hours at 20°C–25°C or overnight at 4°C.
Remove parafilm squares by dipping each slide in PBST to let them float off, then discard parafilm squares.
Wash slides three times (10 minutes per wash) using fresh PBST solutions.
Prepare secondary antibody solution in PBST.
Mix the solution by gently flicking the tube or pipetting up and down.
Repeat steps with secondary antibody in PBST.
Remove parafilm by floating it off.
Wash in a fresh Coplin jar of PBST for 10 min at 20°C–25°C.
Perform click reaction after primary and secondary antibody labeling.
Transfer slides to a fresh Coplin jar of PBS with 1% Triton X for 30 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Prepare Click-iT™ reagents fresh according to the kit’s specifications.
Apply 100 μL of Click-iT™ solution onto parafilm squares and gently touch slides to the liquid.
Place slides in a humid chamber for 30 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Float parafilm squares off and wash slides twice for 5 minutes each in PBST.
Add DAPI (Stock: 5 mg/mL; diluted to 1:10,000) to a Coplin jar of PBST.
Place slides in the DAPI-containing Coplin jar and incubate for 20 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Wash slides for 5 minutes in PBST.
Mount slides using NPG-glycerol or Prolong Glass Antifade Mounting Media.
Pipette approximately 11 μL of NPG-glycerol onto a high-Performance coverslip.
Cut the pipette tip if necessary, as NPG-glycerol is viscous.
Dry the slide using a paper towel to remove excess liquid around the worms without touching the worm carcasses.
Gently touch the slide containing the samples to the mounting media on the coverslip.
Aspirate excess mounting media using a pipette tip connected to a vacuum trap.
Seal the slides with nail polish.
Cure samples for 24 hours at 20°C–25°C in the dark.
Seal slides with nail polish and store them covered at 4°C or -20°C.
Place slide coverslip down by propping it on two slides using a standard dissection microscope.
Locate gonads under the microscope, marking each gonad with a dot or circle using a black pen.
Place slide coverslip down onto a dissecting scope, between two clear slides with tape.
Locate the worm carcasses and mark them with nearby dots.
Mount slide coverslip on your imaging platform using black dots to locate samples.
Image diakinesis stage by locating it at the proximal end of the gonad in DAPI channel.
Check EdU channel visually to ensure correct labeling of samples.
Create a z-stack image covering about 6–7 μm in depth for diakinesis nuclei.
Use diffraction-limited microscopy to observe single sister chromatids.
Repeat steps for imaging all gonads until complete.
Process images according to recommended practices.
Apply ‘Airy Processing’ with default parameters on LSM880.
Perform deconvolution for widefield microscopy processing.
